title: Emmanuel Perez and the Milneburg camp jobs
summary: He played a few weekend jobs with Perez, who was powerful rather than high.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: In regard to Emmanuel Perez, you say you played out at Millenburg? Yeah. How late did they have those camps out at Millenburg? Do you remember about how they were? Do you remember about how late you played with Emmanuel and when they tore it down out there?

Well, the other people in his band at that time, Trombone, who he used. Everyone else. I know it's difficult when you only played maybe a couple of nights. Yeah. The person remembers us who was there 20 or 30 years ago.
The only one I can remember in his line was this Sam drummer. Glass, Henry Glass. That's the only fella I remember that was on that job. How did Perez play?
He's another one I never had the chance to hear him play. How was he? Oh, he was powerful.
Did he have a big range, high notes and low too, or how did he do in that respect?
He didn't go very high, but he was so powerful. Did you ever play with him? He put such force behind it that you'd think it was a high note.
Oh, yeah. Did you play with him how much? Very often? You think he played at Millen.
No, I only played two or three jobs with him at that same place that was on Sunday night or Saturday. I did three or four times with him.
